test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 04 Sept, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The average runs scored by a batsman in 23 matches is 44. In the next 10 matches, the batsman scored an average of 14 runs. Find his average runs scored (rounded off to two decimal places) in all the 33 matches.
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Assume a base **average** of 44 for all 33 matches.

Total deviation in the last 10 matches = 10 × (14 − 44) = −300.

Net change in **average** = −300 ÷ 33 ≈ −9.09.

Final **average runs** = 44 − 9.09 = 34.91.

**∴ The correct answer is 34.91 runs.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Runs in first 23 **matches** = 44 per match

Runs in next 10 **matches** = 14 per match

**Formula Used:**

Total Average = (Total Runs) ÷ (Total Matches)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3f6745d7c82bf070eb41e0e30d934ed8c136eff3ecda6066b1e69b27de709d84.png] 

⇒ Total runs in 23 matches = 23 × 44 = 1012

⇒ Total runs in 10 matches = 10 × 14 = 140

⇒ Total runs in 33 matches = 1012 + 140 = 1152

⇒ Combined Average = 1152 ÷ 33

⇒ Average = 34.9090...

⇒ Average ≈ 34.91

**∴ The correct answer is 34.91 runs.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Formula

When two groups are combined, the total average is calculated as Aₐvg = (n₁a₁ + n₂a₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Relationship between Average and Sum

The Sum of observations is always equal to the Average × Number of observations (Sum = Avg × n).

Deviation Method

New Average = Assumed Average + (Net Deviation ÷ Total Count). This reduces calculation complexity.</p
